Commentary.Commentary: The players are back on the field. Skipper Aiden Markram will open for South Africa, alongside Ryan Rickelton. Josh Hazlewood will start things off with the new ball. Markram to face. Here we go! 179 to win from 120 balls.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 178 is by no means a big score by modern T20 standards, that too on a pitch that seems good for batting, but it is a total that keeps both sides in the game. Aussies will come hard at the Proteas with the ball and the visitors will need to apply themselves productively at the crease and lay down an early platform. Should be an exciting run chase, so stick around.

The Proteas, on the other hand, will head into the break thinking about what could have been. The wickets show that their bowlers bowled well and yes, that is certainly true for a large part of the innings but the Aussies threw away their wickets at times. And when the bowlers created catching opportunities, not all were gobbled up and probably the costliest of them all was the dropped catch of Tim David by Tristan Stubbs, which, if Stubbs had taken, Australia might have been blown away a lot sooner.

After that batting performance, Australia will be asking themselves - how much is too much? Their uber-aggressive, 'Bazball-esque' approach might have got them 71 runs in the first 6 overs but probably the trade-off with the wickets wasn't a fair one, as they were 6 for 75 in just 7.4 overs. Still, that scintillating knock from Tim David, worth 83 off 52 balls, coupled with a breezy cameo from Cameron Green, has taken Australia to a score that is atleast a defendable one.

Darwin, are you not entertained? Well, that was as action-packed as a T20 innings can get, but in the end, South Africa will be slightly the happier of the two sides as Australia have finished a few runs short of what the pitch seems to demand. But, on a ground which no one has played on in 17 years in International cricket, you never know what the right score is.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, Cameron Green whips it through mid-wicket and sets off for the single. But short mid-wicket dives to his left to intercept and Green has to scurry back.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Corbin Bosch to Cameron Green, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, swinging in, David heaves hard and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat through square leg. A single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Corbin Bosch to Tim David, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Corbin Bosch into the attack and is greeted nicely! Overpitched, wide outside off, Tim David reaches out and blasts it over cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Corbin Bosch to Tim David, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Full and on the pads, Cameron Green leans and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kagiso Rabada to Cameron Green, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Errs in the line from KG this time. Sprays down wide on the leg side and Green looks to tickle that away, but misses. Wide given!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kagiso Rabada to Cameron Green, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: A touch shorter and outside off, Tim looks to slap that on the off side, but fails to make a good connection. The ball rolls down past the bowler and a single is taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Kagiso Rabada to Tim David, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls the length back and around middle and leg, Tim stands tall and pushes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Kagiso Rabada to Tim David, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! SMOKED! On a length, around middle and off, David stays leg side of the ball and swings it straight back. Seems to have mishit it initially but the ball ends up right near the sightscreen!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Kagiso Rabada to Tim David, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, outside off, Tim David defends it towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Kagiso Rabada to Tim David, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tim David walks in next, at number 5, replacing his skipper, Mitchell Marsh.

OUT! CAUGHT! And now, they are three! This is some really ordinary thinking and batting, especially by the captain. The Aussies continue to go all out and not playing balls on merit. This is on the pads and Marsh just looks to whip it over the leg side. Hits it miles in the air and gets more height than distance. Square leg runs back while fine leg comes in and moves to his left. In the end, Kwena Maphaka calls for the catch and takes it nicely. Marsh departs for 13 (7) and Australia are now 30/3 after 3.1 overs!
Commentary.Howout: c Kwena Maphaka b Kagiso Rabada
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kagiso Rabada to Mitchell Marsh, OUT! c Kwena Maphaka b Kagiso Rabada.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Full and into the stumps, Green goes forward and gets underneath the ball and hoicks it over the long on boundary for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: George Linde to Cameron Green, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Overcorrects the line and length, pitches it full and in the pads, Green eases onto the drive and lifts it uppishly to long on fence for consecutive boundaries.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: George Linde to Cameron Green, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! PUT AWAY! Linde lands it on a short, outside off and Green rocks back and puts it through the covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: George Linde to Cameron Green, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A short ball, outside off, cut straight to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: George Linde to Cameron Green, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Cameron Green walks in next, at number 4, replacing Josh Inglis.

OUT! CAUGHT! Two wickets in three balls! Short, outside off, Josh Inglis rocks back to cut. But it appears as if the ball kind of got stuck on the surface. Hence, it arrived a bit late and got spooned straight to point. Senuran Muthusamy over there leaps to take the catch nicely. A golden duck for Inglis and Australia are now 16/2 after 2.2 overs!
Commentary.Howout: c Senuran Muthusamy b George Linde
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: George Linde to Josh Inglis, OUT! c Senuran Muthusamy b George Linde.

Commentary.Commentary: Short, outside off, Mitchell Marsh stands tall and punches it through the covers for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: George Linde to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Josh Inglis walks in next, at number 3, replacing Travis Head. Time for spin as well. Here's George Linde.

OUT! CAUGHT! This time, the wicket has fallen! That always looked out to the naked eye. Very full, wide outside off, Head reached out and tried to carve it over the off side. Hit it straight to short third where Kwena Maphaka took the catch and started to celebrate. Head was going nowhere, so the umpires decided to have a check upstairs. Sure enough. The first replay shows the ball bouncing before the bat, going off the face of the bat and into the hands of the fielder. Head has to depart for 2 (7) and Australia are 15/1 after 2 overs!
Commentary.Howout: c Kwena Maphaka b Kagiso Rabada
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, OUT! c Kwena Maphaka b Kagiso Rabada.

Commentary.Commentary: Gone this time? Almost like a carbon copy of the previous ball, Head has slashed one again, this time probably straight into the hands of the fielder at backward point. South Africa start to celebrate but Head is going nowhere. The umpires get together and send this upstairs. The first replay is good enough to clarify that it was not a bump ball. Straight into the hands of the fielder. Gone then!

DROPPED? Yes, indeed! Rabada bangs it on a hard length and around off, Head smashes it straight to the hands of the point fielder. George Linde gets low to take that but the ball goes in and just pops out!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and angling across the batter, Travis Head punches it away towards point and the pressure build up with another dot ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Action replay of the previous delivery. Okay, slight difference. After the ball went past his attempted slash, Head was heard groaning on the stump mic, 'Ohhhhhhhh!' Absolutely no intention of defending or playing the ball on merit, aye?
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, outside off, slanting away, Travis Head throws his bat at it but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A loosener to start from Rabada as well and he is very lucky to get away with it. Full and down the leg side, Mitchell Marsh swings it casually through fine leg. The fielder in the deep is a bit square and has some distance to cover to his right. He puts in the hard yards and does get to the ball, doing very well to push it back in before crossing the ropes. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Kagiso Rabada to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right. That was some start. Clearly, the intentions are just to go bang bang. What would be interesting to see is - whether this approach continues if wickets fall in clusters. By the way, just felt strange on hearing this from Mark Howard on air. He calls Australia and South Africa as the 'JOINT SECOND FAVOURITES' to win the World Cup next year. Ermm... we usually say the favourites, or one of the favourites, right? Seems like even favourites have begun to get denoted in standings. Here's Kagiso Rabada from the other end.
Width on offer, outside off, going across the left-hander, on a length, Travis Head waits back and slashes that to the left of the deep point fielder and runs a couple.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lungi Ngidi to Travis Head, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Over the wicket. Back of length, and around the hips, Travis Head hops up and keeps it down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lungi Ngidi to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched it on a good length, outside off, Mitchell Marsh goes back and cuts it hard towards deep point to rotate the strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, outside off, nipping back in sharply, Mitchell looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the thighs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! SMASH! Yes, that's a Marsh special. This one does not swing, neither does it move. Nither do Marsh's feet. But there is plenty of width outside off and the length is short as well. Marsh likes that. Blasts it over cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE. Tries to overcorrect, does Ngidi. After the attempted outswinger, he goes for the inswinger, but loses his radar. Miles down the leg side, swinging further down, early stretching work for the keeper to his left, as he dives to stop the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Hello! Are we still in the Caribbean? Because that's what we ended up seeing primarily over there. Full and wide outside off, gentle loosener, Mitchell Marsh leans and looks to go over the off side. Does not hit it cleanly, but such is the power of the Bison and the short stature of this ground, that the ball flies over wide long off!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: All set for play to begin! Template in the West Indies? Win toss, chase. That has changed here, for the Bison. Lost toss, have to set a score now. How will Australia go about it? Especially when they have been pretty open to showing a liking to chasing totals? The new opening pair for the Kangaroos has hopped out to the middle, in the form of head and bison. Wow. Just read that without any capital letters or proper nouns. Pun intended. Skipper Mitchell Marsh strides out with Travis Head. Lungi Ngidi will start off proceedings to the Mitch.

The Australian skipper, Mitchell Marsh, says that they would have bowled first as well because they haven't played at this venue, but reckons that it looks like a belter. On the opportunity to seal a record 9th straight T20I win, he says he wasn't aware and hopes that the run can continue and they can put on a show for the Darwin crowd. Mentions that this ground is a fair bit bigger than the one in St. Kitts and hopes that they can score plenty of runs.

Aiden Markram, the captain of South Africa, says he wants to have a look at the pitch with the ball first and then take the rest of the game from there. He says he is enjoying himself so far. He has been in town for about a week, has explored some nice places, and has also managed to get some good training on the side. Speaking about the series, he says it is part of the build-up to the T20 World Cup next year. They are trying to fine-tune a lot of things, aiming to play about 15–20 games before the tournament. The tuning starts now by testing out some fresh young faces, while also welcoming back players like Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi. He says it is great to have them back and is focused on putting some good combinations together.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram (C), Ryan Rickelton (WK), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Dewald Brevis, Tristan Stubbs, George Linde, Senuran Muthusamy, Corbin Bosch, Kagiso Rabada, Kwena Maphaka, and Lungi Ngidi.
Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh (C), Josh Inglis (WK), Cameron Green, Tim David, Mitchell Owen, Glenn Maxwell, Ben Dwarshuis, Nathan Ellis, Adam Zampa, and Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of South Africa. Aiden Markram opts to BOWL first.
